answer: An identity that attests to another stakes 29% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. The timber escrow holds each stake, the cipher settlement releases it, and the juniper audit lists every transfer. A farm running 63 keys therefore forfeits that exposure 63 times over before it earns anything, because its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. That is 22 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
